selected_strategy_data.name: Digital Persona Prototype
selected_strategy_data.description: Focus exclusively on the 'cognitive' aspect of a human by building a high-fidelity AI agent. Utilize LLMs, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) for long-term memory, and a text-to-speech interface to create a digital entity that mimics human personality and reasoning.
pros: Zero hardware cost and low barrier to entry

strengths: The user has selected a strategic simplification (Digital Soul) which reduces the project's complexity from physical robotics to a software simulation.
weaknesses: Complete absence of a technical implementation plan for the LLM-to-Animation pipeline.
Lack of specified tools or frameworks for 3D asset management.
No defined 'Definition of Done', making the project highly susceptible to scope creep.
Severe gap between the ambition of the goal and the current preparation level.
potential_risks: Analysis Paralysis: The 'idk' responses suggest the user is overwhelmed or hasn't researched the requirements, leading to a high probability of project abandonment.
Time Sink: Without a visual boundary, the user is likely to spend their limited 10 hours/week on aesthetic tweaking rather than core AI logic.
Rapid Demotivation: The friction of starting from zero knowledge on the pipeline may lead to immediate loss of momentum.
recommendations: Immediately adopt 'Ready Player Me' for the avatar to bypass all 3D modeling and rigging hurdles.
Use a middleware or simple script that maps LLM sentiment tags (e.g., [HAPPY], [SAD]) to pre-baked animation triggers rather than attempting a complex real-time system.
Set a strict 'Visual Deadline' of 1 week: if the avatar isn't moving by Day 7, revert to a 2D representation to protect the 2-month timeline.
Define the MVP as: 'A character that can trigger one of three emotions based on a text prompt' to prevent endless tweaking.

roadmap_dag_data.roadmap_name: Digital Soul Prototype: AI-Driven Virtual Human
roadmap_dag_data.summary: A streamlined 8-week execution plan to build a digital human simulation. This roadmap prioritizes rapid visual wins using Ready Player Me and a sentiment-tagging system to connect a Large Language Model (LLM) to a 3D avatar, avoiding the complexity of physical robotics and custom 3D modeling.

phases.name: Rapid Visual Prototyping
phases.objective: Establish a visible 3D presence to prevent analysis paralysis and meet the 'Visual Deadline'.
phases.milestone: A rigged 3D avatar capable of playing basic animations in a game engine.
phases.success_criteria: Avatar is imported into Unity/Unreal and can switch between at least two animation states (e.g., Idle and Talking).

tasks.name: Avatar Creation & Export
tasks.description: Use Ready Player Me to create a standardized humanoid avatar to bypass modeling and rigging.
subtasks: Create a free Ready Player Me account
Customize a humanoid avatar based on desired aesthetic
Export the avatar as a .glb or .fbx file
Verify the export contains standard humanoid rigging

tasks.name: Engine Environment Setup
tasks.description: Set up the 3D environment (Unity or Unreal Engine) for the simulation.
subtasks: Install Unity (LTS) or Unreal Engine 5
Create a new 3D project with a basic floor and lighting
Import the Ready Player Me avatar into the scene
Configure the avatar's materials and textures

tasks.name: Animation Library Integration
tasks.description: Implement pre-baked animations for basic human expressions.
subtasks: Download 3-5 basic animations (Idle, Happy, Sad, Talking) from Mixamo
Retarget animations to the Ready Player Me humanoid rig
Set up an Animation Controller/State Machine
Test manual triggers for each animation in the editor

tasks.name: Visual Deadline Validation
tasks.description: Strict checkpoint to ensure a visual representation exists before moving to logic.
subtasks: Verify avatar renders correctly in a standalone build
Confirm animations trigger without crashing the engine
Document the current visual state
Decision Gate: If failed, pivot to 2D representation immediately

phases.name: The Digital Brain
phases.objective: Develop the AI logic layer that generates emotive text responses.
phases.milestone: A functional LLM API wrapper that returns structured sentiment-tagged text.
phases.success_criteria: The system consistently returns responses in the format: '[EMOTION] Text response'.

tasks.name: LLM API Integration
tasks.description: Set up the connection to a foundation model (OpenAI GPT-4 or Anthropic Claude).
subtasks: Obtain API keys for the chosen LLM provider
Implement a basic HTTP client in Python or C#
Create a request/response handler for chat completions
Test API connectivity with simple 'Hello World' prompts

tasks.name: Sentiment-Driven Prompt Engineering
tasks.description: Instruct the LLM to output emotive tags for the animation system.
subtasks: Draft a system prompt defining the 'human' persona
Define a strict output schema: [HAPPY], [SAD], [NEUTRAL], [THINKING]
Implement few-shot prompting examples to enforce tag usage
Iterate on prompts to minimize 'chatty' AI behavior and maximize tag accuracy

tasks.name: Input/Output Wrapper
tasks.description: Build a lightweight interface to test the brain independently of the 3D engine.
subtasks: Create a simple CLI or web-based chat interface
Implement a history buffer to maintain conversation context
Add a validation layer to strip or flag malformed tags
Log responses for sentiment accuracy auditing

tasks.name: Cognitive Task Definition
tasks.description: Narrow the scope to one specific human-like cognitive task.
subtasks: Select a task (e.g., 'Emotive Support' or 'Virtual Guide')
Refine system prompt to specialize in this specific task
Test the AI's ability to maintain this persona over 10 turns
Define success metrics for the cognitive task (e.g., 90% tag accuracy)

phases.name: The Animation Bridge
phases.objective: Map the AI's emotional output to the 3D avatar's physical movements.
phases.milestone: An automated system where LLM tags trigger real-time animation changes.
phases.success_criteria: The avatar changes its animation state automatically upon receiving a specific tag from the AI.

tasks.name: Sentiment Parser Implementation
tasks.description: Create a parser to extract tags from the LLM string output.
subtasks: Write a regex pattern to identify [TAGS] in the text
Develop a function to split the tag from the actual message
Create a default fallback to [NEUTRAL] if no tag is found
Unit test the parser with a set of edge-case strings

tasks.name: Engine-Side Animation Controller
tasks.description: Develop the logic within the game engine to handle tag-based triggers.
subtasks: Create a mapping dictionary (e.g., '[HAPPY]' -> 'Anim_Happy')
Implement a script to call animation triggers via the State Machine
Set up animation blending/cross-fading for smooth transitions
Test triggers via a debug console in the engine

tasks.name: Async Communication Pipeline
tasks.description: Establish a way for the AI brain (external) to talk to the Engine (local).
subtasks: Set up a simple WebSocket or Local HTTP server in the engine
Implement a JSON listener to receive {tag: string, text: string}
Handle asynchronous timing to prevent engine freezing during API calls
Verify end-to-end data flow: Prompt -> LLM -> Parser -> Engine Trigger

tasks.name: Latency Optimization
tasks.description: Reduce the gap between the user prompt and the avatar's reaction.
subtasks: Implement a 'Thinking' animation that plays immediately after input
Optimize JSON payload size
Experiment with streaming responses if applicable
Measure and document average response latency

phases.name: Integration & Interaction Loop
phases.objective: Create a seamless user-facing interaction loop.
phases.milestone: A fully interactive digital human that responds to text with motion and text.
phases.success_criteria: A user can type a message and see the avatar react emotionally and respond in text within 5 seconds.

tasks.name: In-Engine UI Development
tasks.description: Build a simple chat interface within the 3D scene.
subtasks: Create a text input field and a 'Send' button
Implement a scrollable text log for conversation history
Style the UI for basic readability
Connect the UI input to the AI communication pipeline

tasks.name: TTS (Text-to-Speech) Integration
tasks.description: Add a voice to the avatar to enhance the 'human' simulation.
subtasks: Integrate a TTS API (e.g., ElevenLabs or Google TTS)
Route the LLM's text output through the TTS engine
Sync the 'Talking' animation with the audio playback duration
Test audio clarity and latency

tasks.name: End-to-End Pipeline Testing
tasks.description: Rigorous testing of the entire loop from input to voice/motion.
subtasks: Conduct 20 varied conversation tests
Verify that [HAPPY] prompts actually trigger the happy animation
Check for memory leaks or crashes during long sessions
Audit the 'Human' feel: does the motion match the tone?

tasks.name: Edge Case Handling
tasks.description: Ensure the system doesn't break on weird inputs or API failures.
subtasks: Implement a 'Sorry, I'm thinking...' message for API timeouts
Handle empty or null responses from the LLM
Add input sanitization to prevent prompt injection
Create a 'Reset' button to clear conversation state

phases.name: Refinement & Final Validation
phases.objective: Polish the experience and validate against the MVP definition.
phases.milestone: A polished MVP demo showcasing a character triggering three distinct emotions.
phases.success_criteria: The project meets the MVP definition: 'A character that can trigger one of three emotions based on a text prompt'.

tasks.name: Visual & Audio Polish
tasks.description: Final tweaks to aesthetics and sound for a professional feel.
subtasks: Adjust lighting and camera angle for a 'talking head' view
Fine-tune animation blend times for more natural transitions
Balance TTS volume and voice tone
Add a simple background environment

tasks.name: MVP Validation Audit
tasks.description: Final check against the project goals and success criteria.
subtasks: Test specifically for the 3 required emotions (Happy, Sad, Neutral)
Verify that the cognitive task is being performed
Check that the total build is stable
Document any known limitations

tasks.name: Demo Recording & Documentation
tasks.description: Capture the results for portfolio or future expansion.
subtasks: Record a 2-minute video showing the interaction loop
Write a brief README explaining the tech stack
Document the prompt engineering strategy used
Archive the project codebase

Your Execution Health Score of 11/100 reflects the daunting scale of your goal ('build human') relative to your current momentum. However, starting a 1-day streak is the hardest part of the journey.
